subject: Core Mathematics
topic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids

unit.substrand: Sub-Strand 2.7: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
unit.sep: Use nets/cross-sections,decompose boundaries/volumes,model capacity and verify units/limits.
unit.careers: Illustrative packaging,storage,material planning and design contexts;no qualification/current-price claims.
unit.focus: Distinguish exposed surfaces from internal volume across prisms,pyramids,cones,frustums,spheres and composites.
unit.phenomenon: A design team agrees on a shape but disagrees about how much covering material or storage space it needs.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Dimensioned nets,similar-cone cuts,joined cap interfaces,cavities and ideal container estimates.
unit.drivingQuestion: Which surface or space does this decision actually require us to measure? KICD: How do we determine the surface area and volume of solids? Why do we determine the surface area and volume of solids?
unit.storylineThread: Prism/pyramid/cone/frustum/sphere surfaces → composite boundary → prism/pointed/frustum/sphere volumes → composite space → application → critique → independent commission.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner uses a cylinder and a cone of the same radius and height, and a substance such as sand or water, to determine the volume of a cone as a third of the volume of a cylinder.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner uses a cylinder and a cone of the same radius and height, and a substance such as sand or water, to determine the volume of a cone as a third of the volume of a cylinder.
unit.values:
Unity: the learner discusses in a group and establishes the relationship between the volume of a cone and the volume of a cylinder.
Respect: the learner listens to others’ opinions as they discuss in groups and work out the volumes of prisms, pyramids, cones, frustums and spheres.
unit.pcis: Environment and technology: as the learner collects and uses containers from the immediate environment and use them to discuss and work out their volumes.
unit.content: Surface Area of Solids; Volume of Solids

assessment.subjectLabel: SURFACE AREA AND VOLUME OF SOLIDS
assessment.instructions: Lesson 14:3 minutes procedure,20 minutes sections 1–2,11 minutes sections 3–4,2 minutes private check/limitation reflection and 4 minutes final checking/collection,total 40. Work independently with SV14 and a scientific calculator. Show which faces/solid parts are included,formulas,working and units. Give exactπ forms where appropriate and final approximations to 3 decimal places when requested. Formula support is allowed;no teaching cards. This written task does not certify physical making/measuring.

sections.title: 1. A closed frustum
sections.prompt: For F,calculate total exposed surface area and volume exactly and approximately. Explain which circular ends are included and why vertical height 4,not slant 5,belongs in the volume formula. Give one geometric/data check.
sections.exemplar: Curved 45π plus ends 36π+9π gives 90π≈282.743 cm². V=(4π/3)(36+18+9)=84π≈263.894 cm³. Both circular ends are exposed because the frustum is closed. Volume uses perpendicular height 4;slant 5 belongs to curved surface. Check 5²=4²+(6−3)² or a valid bounding-cylinder/positive-area check.

sections.title: 2. A capped cylinder
sections.prompt: For G,identify exposed faces and compute total surface area and volume exactly and approximately. Explain why the joined disks do not count as external surfaces,and why their contact area is not subtracted as a volume.
sections.exemplar: Exposed area cylinder side 24π+hemisphere curved 8π+bottom 4π=36π≈113.097 cm². V=cylinder 24π+hemisphere 16π/3=88π/3≈92.153 cm³. Joining disks are internal;the two solids touch at a plane rather than overlap in 3 D volume. Do not add a top-cylinder base or a hemisphere flat base to external area.

sections.title: 3. Capacity and the stated dimensions
sections.prompt: Find H’s capacity in cm³ and litres. Explain why the specification says internal dimensions and what information would be missing if only outside dimensions were supplied.
sections.exemplar: 25×12×8=2400 cm³=2.4 L. Capacity uses available inside space;outside dimensions alone do not provide wall thickness/internal geometry. Do not silently equate an outside box volume with usable capacity.

sections.title: 4. Explore a practical design decision
sections.prompt: Choose F or G as a proposed ideal container. Explain one use of its computed surface area and one use of its volume. Name one further datum/assumption needed for actual material/capacity planning,and describe a safe next step to explore the design. Do not invent a price or claim a measurement you did not perform.
sections.exemplar: Surface area can estimate intended covering/material quantity;volume can estimate ideal storage space. Real planning might need internal/external dimensions,wall thickness,joining/cutting allowance,measurement precision or an applicable price. A safe next step is an accurately labelled paper model or teacher-approved measurement of a clean stable container,recording actual versus assumed dimensions. Judge explicit quantity-to-use reasoning,not a particular decoration or physical action inferred from writing.

rubric.criterion: Determine and justify basic/composite exposed surface areas
rubric.excellent: Both exact/approximate areas and exposed-face inventories are correct;clearly explains all included/hidden faces with consistent square units.
rubric.proficient: Correctly calculates both areas and explains the exposed ends/hidden joined disks.
rubric.developing: Identifies relevant surfaces but a face count,calculation or unit needs correction.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided support to distinguish exposed surface from full standalone component surfaces.

rubric.criterion: Determine and interpret basic/composite volume and capacity
rubric.excellent: All volumes/capacity conversions are correct;clearly distinguishes perpendicular/slant height,zero-thickness contact and internal space with valid checks.
rubric.proficient: Correctly calculates both solid volumes and capacity,with appropriate height,contact and internal-dimension explanations.
rubric.developing: A sensible model is present but a volume,conversion,height or contact explanation is incomplete.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided support to choose component volumes and distinguish area from volume/capacity.

rubric.criterion: Explore a practical use with explicit limits
rubric.excellent: Clearly connects both quantities to distinct planning uses,identifies a relevant missing input and gives a safe,concrete evidence-gathering step without overclaiming.
rubric.proficient: Explains relevant area/volume uses,a missing datum/assumption and a safe next step.
rubric.developing: A relevant use is present but quantity,limit or next step is vague.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs prompts to connect a geometric quantity to a practical decision and evidence need.
